content: A Russian SU-27 fighter jet aggressively approached a US RC-135U intelligence-gathering plane in international airspace over the Sea of Okhotsk on April 23, maneuvering in a way that demonstrated it was armed with air-to-air missiles.
Prince Charles and his wife Camilla will embark on a 12-day tour of Australia and New Zealand, visiting 12 towns and cities, including meeting the new Australian PM Malcolm Turnbull.
A man in his 70s has been detained and is being questioned at a Garda station in Killarney, Ireland, in connection with a September attack on a woman in Sneem, County Kerry.

A former GP, Hugh McGoldrick, had his name erased from the medical register after a Medical Practitioners Tribunal hearing, as no appeal was made within the 28-day deadline following his conviction for falsifying drug trials.
A 21-year-old male has been arrested on suspicion of murder in Dorking, Surrey, while police await the results of a post-mortem examination.

A 21-year-old man, Josh Hanson, was stabbed to death at a bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon, early Sunday morning, and Scotland Yard is urging around 40 people who were present at the time to come forward with information.
Hovertravel, a cross-Solent ferry service, is considering adding a new route between Sandown and Southsea, operating on two days a week in July and August, to boost tourism on the Isle of Wight.
Police are investigating an early Sunday morning attack in the Heights area where a victim was reportedly assaulted by up to eight men, and a 30-year-old suspect has been released on bail.
The death toll from the floods in India has doubled to over 200 with over 100 bodies found as waters recede, affecting 450,000 people in the state.

Arsenal will host Leicester City on Friday 11 August to kick off the 25th anniversary season of the Premier League, with Sky Sports awarded the rights to screen the match as part of their multi-million pound deal.

Oldham Athletic Football Club has dismissed Cristian Montano, a 22-year-old player, following an investigation into spot-fixing allegations, despite the player being bailed by the National Crime Agency until April 2014.
A 20-year-old man, Rick Edwards, was given a suspended 12-month jail term and a supervision order after admitting to starting a fire at the former Pontins resort in Brixham for "fun" in 2014.
Former Forest player Wilson has been without a team since being released in May, having previously made 51 appearances in his second spell at the club after rejoining from Celtic in 2013.
Australia's Matthew Wade scored 76 as Sri Lanka won the second match of the five-match series by 82 runs, levelling the series at 1-1.

Sale Sharks forward Vadim Cobilas has signed with French Top 14 team Bordeaux, leaving Sale at the end of his contract, with the club's boss Steve Diamond also in advanced talks with other players over new deals.

India's chase of 349 against Australia collapsed after a strong start, with both Shikhar Dhawan and Virat Kohli making centuries, but ultimately falling short as Australia's pace bowler Kane Richardson took 5-68, leading Australia to a 4-0 series lead.

The Hammersmith and City Line and parts of the Circle Line have been suspended due to concerns over debris falling onto the tracks following a major fire at a 24-storey block in London, at the request of the London Fire Brigade.
Jamie Hamill, a 27-year-old Scottish footballer, has signed a three-year contract to rejoin Kilmarnock, where he will make his second debut and reach his 150th appearance for the club.
Ipswich fan Ross Morgan accidentally punched a hole in his ceiling while celebrating a goal by Paul Anderson, but was surprised and grateful when Anderson offered to pay for the repairs.

In Wales, new laws have been implemented requiring retailers to keep cigarettes out of public view, with shop managers and assistants facing fines of up to £5,000 and six months in prison if they fail to comply.
Bristol Rovers has re-signed 20-year-old Lucas, who previously made 10 appearances for the team this season, scoring three goals, and is expected to provide options in the forward areas.
Network Rail is undertaking maintenance work at Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire, including repairing the station to make it watertight and rebuilding the signal box's chimney stack.

Lawrence Phillips, a former NFL player, has been found dead, with officials believing he took his own life, despite being accused of killing his former cellmate and having a history of troubled behavior and multiple convictions.

The Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT) plan proposes extending bus lane operating hours from 07:30-09:30 and 15:30-18:30 to 07:00-19:00, with a potential for flexible loading and unloading windows through community consultation.
Lionel Messi scored the winner in Barcelona's 2-1 victory over Atletico, marking his 287th La Liga goal and extending his lead as the competition's all-time top scorer.

In a major match-fixing scandal in Italy, over 70 people, including players, directors, and club officials from around 30 lower-division clubs, are under investigation for suspected "conspiracy to commit sporting fraud", with links to the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate believed to be involved.

Approximately 1,600 Dolomedes plantarius spiderlings, a hybrid species created by combining spiders from Sussex and Suffolk, have been released into a dyke at Castle Marshes to establish a new population that can better adapt to its surroundings and climate change.
The article refers to the Partition of India, a historical event in 2017 where two new countries gained independence from British rule, resulting in millions of people becoming refugees.

Iva Barr, a 20th-time marathon participant who started her running career in 1981, completed about 14 miles of the London Marathon before taking a train and walking the final part, describing the experience as "wonderful" despite not finishing the traditional way.

In China's top cities, the extremely high demand for property has led some couples to undergo fake divorces in order to buy additional homes, despite the central bank's efforts to control rising prices.
A 46-year-old landlord, Mr Jones, died at a pub in Holyhead, and a 24-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murder after a stand-off with police.
There is no article provided to summarize. The text appears to be a promotional message with contact information for the BBC News Entertainment team.

A fatal car crash occurred on the A713 road near Carsphairn, Scotland, where a red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van collided, resulting in the deaths of both drivers, Antony Sztuka and Scott Kennedy.
Australian rower Sarah Tait, who won an Olympic silver medal in the women's pair, was remembered as an inspirational and influential role model after being diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013.

In the midst of a new agreement allowing US troops to stay in Afghanistan after 2014, two bomb attacks in Kabul, claimed by the Taliban, injured several people, including soldiers and civilians, and destroyed a bus, amid a backdrop of ongoing conflict and a disputed unity deal between Afghan president Ashraf Ghani and runner-up Abdullah Abdullah.

Daimler, the parent company of Mercedes-Benz, reported a 6% increase in second-quarter sales, with a predicted full-year sales figure of "significantly more than 100bn euros," despite a slowdown in sales growth in China.

A 10-year-old son of Crown Prince Frederik of Denmark was rescued by a lifeguard, Nick Malcolm, from a rip current at Mermaid Beach on the Gold Coast, after officials initially downplayed the incident.
A fire at a residence in Elgin Road, near Inchbroom Road, resulted in the discovery of the body of an elderly man, with police stating that there appear to be no suspicious circumstances.

Veterans with amputation-related medical issues can now receive specialized treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) in Surrey, UK, after a new clinic was established to provide the best possible care for those who have made sacrifices for Britain's safety.

In Port Talbot, Wales, four average speed cameras on the M4 have caught around 125 drivers per day exceeding the speed limit in the first week of operation, a decrease from the 700 daily catches during a pilot period.

A Manchester-born teacher, arrested in Spain as part of an Interpol investigation, is suspected of secretly taking photographs of his underage students and possessing a large number of sexually explicit files involving minors.
A sturgeon named Steve, who escaped from a Hampshire aquarium during floods in February, has been found safe and relatively unharmed in a puddle near a car wash about a mile away.
Comedian Chris Rock has filed for divorce from his wife of 19 years, Malaak Compton-Rock, and is requesting privacy as he and his wife work through the process together.
A motorway collision at Tamnamore has caused the road to be closed in both directions, resulting in traffic tailbacks, and police are advising motorists to exit at designated junctions.

The Vatican has yet to respond to France's nomination of senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini as its new ambassador, with observers suggesting that the long silence may indicate a rejection of the proposal.
The Nasdaq index plummeted 2.4% to close at 4,876, its largest one-day fall since April 10 last year, despite Kraft Foods shares surging over 35% after a merger announcement.

Marketa Vondrousova and Borna Coric won their respective titles, with Vondrousova defeating Kaia Kanepi in the final and Coric saving five match points to defeat Philipp Kohlschreiber in the Grand Prix Hassan II.
Stoke City has signed 28-year-old Cameroonian forward Eric Choupo-Moting as their fourth summer signing, with the player having a significant experience in the Bundesliga and international football.

A 56-year-old man with cerebral palsy, Seamus McCollum, died at a private nursing home in Randalstown, Maine, but it wasn't until an April autopsy that his death was investigated as a potential murder.
Heavy rains in Tamil Nadu, India, and neighboring Sri Lanka have caused widespread flooding, with thousands evacuated and a relief fund of 5 billion rupees announced to aid affected areas.

A McGill's bus caught fire on the A760 Kilbirnie Road near Largs on Saturday, but thanks to the quick actions of the driver, all passengers, including a partially-sighted mother, were safely evacuated and uninjured.

Notts County cricketer Jake Ball, who has taken six wickets in each of the team's first two County Championship matches, is currently the leading wicket-taker in Division One and has impressed coaches with his strong early-season performances.

Jersey unveiled a memorial stone in the French village of Guillemont to honor the island's role in World War I, with a portion of the stone being returned to Jersey to become part of a monument in Royal Square.

John Boyega, who played stormtrooper Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens, visited his former theatre company, Theatre Peckham, where he was a member from age nine to 14, to give back to the community as a graduate.
Luke Donald carded a 65 to move within four strokes of the lead at the European tour event, with 16 players within five shots of the top spot.

Middlesex finished the first day of their County Championship match against Hampshire in a strong position, with Adam Voges remaining unbeaten on 128 and the team reaching 342-3, thanks in large part to Voges and Dawid Malan's 279-run partnership.

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy is in critical condition after an incident in Penilee Road, with police having located a 54-year-old man they wanted to speak to in the Dumfries and Galloway area.

A three-bedroom house in Wavertree, where a young member of The Beatles lived from birth until age five, has been sold at auction to an anonymous telephone bidder for an undisclosed price within the guide range of £150,000 to £250,000.

A 52-year-old man, David Ellam, died after being attacked by a dog near his home in Huddersfield, and a 29-year-old man, Aaron Joseph, has been charged with owning a dog that was dangerously out of control at the time of the incident.
A 22-year-old man from Shrewsbury, Thomas Bebbington, has been found dead after his body was discovered on private land near Leighton, approximately 10 miles from the town center.
Five-week-old baby otters are doing well and are expected to be moved to a large outdoor enclosure with a pool and fed live food by the summer.
Police in Newtownards are seeking witnesses to a bonfire disturbance on Monday and potential activity around a home where 33-year-old Joanne Thompson was found deceased on Wednesday.
A record-breaking 2,270 black-tailed godwits spent time on the island of Tiree this spring, with many stopping to refuel before their migration to Iceland.
Rangers manager Mark Warburton has decided not to retain youth coach Ian Durrant, who had previously spent 14 years as a player and several years as a coach at the club.
A rare albino deer has been born, with biologists estimating that such occurrences happen only once every 100,000 births.

Asad Khan, a 14-year-old student from Bradford, died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heaton School, with his family claiming he had been bullied, and an inquest is ongoing to investigate the circumstances of his death.

A painting depicting the 1654 coronation ceremony, which has been in Rokeby Park since at least 1880, has been restored and is now being studied to determine its origin and value, despite experts being unable to identify the artist.
Macclesfield Town secured a 3-0 win over Wrexham, with goals from Danny Rowe, Mitch Hancox, and Danny Whittaker, lifting them up to seventh in the table.

French oil and gas company Total has partnered with the Confederation of African Football (Caf) as the new headline sponsor of 10 competitions, including the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations finals in Gabon.

Spain's coach Lopetegui has selected a squad for their first World Cup qualifier, recalling players such as Diego Costa and Juan Mata, while Casillas has been overlooked for the matches against Belgium and Liechtenstein.

A large wildfire, believed to have been started deliberately, has spread across a 5-kilometre area in a region near the border, with authorities appealing to the public to stop reckless behaviour that is putting lives and property at risk.

Former English cricketer Boyd Rankin has announced his return to Ireland's national team, citing a desire to be part of Ireland's potential bid for Test status and to play in the upcoming ICC World Twenty20 in India.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, created with the Patient Client Council, aims to provide an independent voice and improve treatment and care for individuals and families affected by rare diseases in Northern Ireland.

Gloucester Cathedral plans to introduce girl choristers to its choir, which was established in 1539, with the aim of discovering talented young girls from local schools and backgrounds to join the cathedral's musical worship.
Pedro, a 29-year-old Chelsea winger, suffered a head injury, including a concussion, in a game in Beijing, but is expected to be okay and will wear a protective mask upon returning to training.
Nottinghamshire has appointed James Taylor and David Sales as coaches, with Taylor bringing his one-day cricket expertise and Sales offering technical advice to the county's batsmen.
A man has been charged with several offenses, including assault on police, after an incident on Whiterock Road in Belfast on Friday afternoon.
A volunteer crew from the Larne RNLI successfully towed a yacht to safety at Carrick Marina after its engine failed in good weather conditions, with the assistance of two lifeboats.
Ipswich Town secured a 3-2 win over MK Dons, with Mick McCarthy's side overcoming a comeback attempt by the visitors, who are struggling to move on from a disappointing season.

A man from Darlington has been issued a summons to appear in court on charges of dangerous driving and causing serious injury after a bridge collapsed onto a London-bound motorway, injuring a motorcyclist.

A flashmob in Platja d'Aro, Spain, involving around 200 people, turned into a panic when bystanders mistook selfie sticks for weapons, leading to 11 people being treated for injuries and police responding to false reports of shots being fired.

Two people, Sindyann Regis and Chevaze Mcgregor, have been charged with the murder of 2-year-old Jeremiah Regis, who was found with over 100 injuries, including a bite to the chest, and died from blunt force trauma.

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common in the UK has engulfed a significant area, prompting the deployment of 20 fire engine crews and a police helicopter, with firefighters expected to remain on the scene overnight due to challenging conditions.
An agreement has been reached to keep Leicester Speedway club going, with a 15-year lease signed for the team's venue at Beaumont Park.
A 50-year-old woman, Elizabeth Bowe, was found badly injured in St Andrews and later died, and her brother, Charles Gordon, 51, has been charged with her murder and remanded in custody.
Ross County has signed 29-year-old midfielder Jim O'Brien on a two-year contract, bringing him back to the club after a successful six-month loan stint last season.
Northants took control of the match against Durham, restricting the hosts to 59-3 and 107 runs behind, with their seam attack exposing Durham's fragile batting line-up.

New Zealand's Ko, along with Canadian Brooke Henderson and South Korean Lee Mi-rim, are joint leaders at two under par after two rounds at the women's major in Seattle, with Scotland's Catriona Matthew three shots behind.
Former Scotland coach Alex McLeish's assistant, Gordon Watson, has rejoined the Scotland national team as an assistant to manager Gordon Strachan, alongside Mark McGhee, for the World Cup qualifiers.

The Belfast Giants secured a 5-3 win over the Cardiff Devils, with goals from Colin Shields, Ryan Martinelli, Mark Garside, Alex Foster, and Steve Saviano, while the Devils will look to close the gap with upcoming matches.
At the 2016 Masters, Jordan Spieth, the defending champion, suffered a quadruple-bogey on the 12th hole, ultimately leading to his collapse and allowing Danny Willett to win the tournament.
The BBC is inviting viewers to share their photographs of England through various social media platforms, with guidelines provided for submitting and using the images.

An optometrist, Honey Rose, is on trial for gross negligence manslaughter, accused of failing to properly conduct a routine eye test that led to the death of a patient, Vinnie Barker, five months after the test in July 2012.
China's food price inflation rose to 4.9% in June, a figure above analysts' expectations but still below the government's target of 3.5%, which may reduce the prospect of interest rate cuts in 2013.
Ivory Coast international and former Newcastle player Cheick Tiote, 30, died after collapsing during training with Chinese second-tier side Beijing Enterprises on June 5.
Slovak Peter Sagan won the fifth stage of the Tour de France, with Thibaut Pinot moving into second place overall behind leader Nairo Quintana.

Cuadrilla's plans to frack at its Preston New Road site in Lancashire have been approved, despite an ongoing legal challenge, and the company has pledged to prioritize the county's economy by creating jobs and investing in local initiatives.

Three teenagers from north-west London, who were suspected of planning to travel to Syria, were arrested in Turkey and later released without charge in the UK after being detained at Istanbul's airport.

A respiratory consultant at the Royal Berkshire Hospital has criticized the £22.95 quote for a blackout blind, suggesting that the price was excessive, and the hospital has stated that the quote was reviewed and rejected.
Swansea's development squad won the league crown in March and secured 31 wins across all competitions in the 2016-17 season, culminating in a cup final victory.

Denbighshire councillors are considering creating a secondary dune system to strengthen defences at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, following severe storms in December 2013 that caused damage to the existing dune system and resulted in flooding affecting hundreds of properties.

South Shields, a team from the eighth tier of English football, will host a live broadcast of a match from the 2017-18 FA Cup tournament on August 19, with commentary provided by Conor McNamara and Danny Webber.

Police in Scotland are investigating a targeted attack on a property in which a 38-year-old man suffered serious facial injuries, while a 49-year-old man present at the scene did not require medical attention.
A 51-year-old woman, Pamela McLaggan, has pleaded guilty to manslaughter after a 44-year-old man, Jonathan Baines, was found dead at a house in Gainsborough.

A 15-year-old boy was assaulted at Patterton station on October 3, punched from behind and stamped on, suffering facial injuries, and his mobile phone was stolen, with British Transport Police appealing for witnesses from a train service that arrived at Neilston at 23:40.

Two 17-year-old boys, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, from Dewsbury, are being investigated by West Yorkshire Police and counter-terrorism officers for allegedly traveling to Syria to join the Islamic State in March.
The Great Britain ice hockey team has announced a 22-man squad for the upcoming 2016 Olympic qualifying tournament, featuring several familiar faces from their 2015 World Championship roster.
Matthew Perry is set to appear in a tribute to James Burrows, the creator of Friends, alongside his former co-stars, but it is not a reunion episode.
Jones, a 31-year-old footballer who started his career at Manchester United, made 41 league appearances last season to help his club, Burnley, win the Championship title.
A lawyer, Joe Acquaro, was found shot dead in Melbourne, and investigators suspect that underworld bosses may have put a price on his head, possibly linked to his work with clients involved in crime.

Air France flight AF374, carrying 294 passengers from Paris to Vancouver, was diverted to Glasgow Prestwick after a slight smell of burning was detected on board, and a second aircraft was sent to fly the passengers back to Paris.

A yellow severe weather warning has been issued for Britain as the remains of Hurricane Gonzalo are expected to bring strong winds and heavy rain, particularly affecting coastal areas and north-western parts of Wales.
The article explores the issue of overcrowding in hospitals and its potential impact on children who require urgent medical attention.

A 64-year-old man, Kenneth David Dickie, died from a head injury sustained at Rockley Park in Poole, and two individuals, a 34-year-old man and a 57-year-old woman, have been charged and bailed in connection with his death.

Former Manchester United forward Matteo Macheda will stay with Nottingham Forest at the City Ground until the end of the season, having joined the club despite not being a regular starter for his previous team, Cardiff.

The body of Christopher Huxtable, a 34-year-old man from Swansea who had been missing since a building collapse in February, was finally found and recovered from the site, bringing closure to his family, although two other men, Ken Cresswell and John Shaw, remain missing.

Bristol City head coach Lee Johnson emphasizes the importance of their upcoming match against QPR, highlighting the potential for a win to significantly improve their chances of catching up with teams above them in the league.

Luca, an ESA astronaut, described walking in space as "absolutely fantastic" after participating in a 2013 mission to the International Space Station, where he performed two spacewalks and traveled over 110 million kilometers.

Joe Arundel, a former England Knights player, has joined Hull FC, expressing excitement and nerves about the new challenge, as the club aims to build a culture and winning mentality with promising young players like him.

Ulster Bank, a subsidiary of RBS, has experienced a payment processing issue affecting around 600,000 customers, but has identified and fixed the problem, with customers advised to contact the bank for assistance.
Tanzania secured a 2-1 victory over Kenya in their 2016 Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, while Ethiopia defeated Uganda 4-1 in a separate play-off for third place.
Due to industrial action in the US affecting potato supplies, McDonald's Japan is rationing French fries by serving only small portions at their over 3,100 outlets.

The total purse for the 2024 Derby has increased to £1.625m with the addition of new entrants, while John Jenkins has defended his decision to run long-shot filly Diore Lia, a 1,000-1 outsider, in the prestigious race.
Atletico Madrid's top scorer, Antoine Griezmann, will miss France's friendly against Ivory Coast due to a haematoma on his left foot, but an X-ray ruled out a bone injury.

Veteran rugby league player Willie Mason, a 35-year-old former NRL player with 290 games under his belt, has joined the Super League's Dragons, bringing his physical and aggressive playing style to the team.
A recent survey by The Marine Conservation Society found an 11% increase in dog mess on UK beaches overall, with a 71% increase in Scotland, but also reported a decrease in overall litter levels.
The UK Supreme Court ruled that government-introduced fees for employment cases, which led to a significant reduction in claims, were indirectly discriminatory to women and thus unlawful.

Wycombe won the match against Dagenham & Redbridge, coming from behind to take the lead twice and ultimately securing the victory through Paris Cowan-Hall's header, as Dagenham remain in the relegation places.

Bee-eaters, a species native to southern Europe, have successfully bred in the UK for a second consecutive summer, with over 1,000 people visiting an RSPB viewpoint to witness the birds' nesting activity at Low Gelt Quarry.
A boy jumped into the River Wey in Guildford to try and save his father after the man's boat capsized, but members of the public intervened and divers are now searching for the missing kayaker.

A young girl was fatally injured by a stone thrown by an elephant at Rabat Zoo in Morocco, with the zoo stating that the incident was rare and unpredictable despite meeting international safety standards.

Labour MP Laura Glass has been appointed to the shadow cabinet, replacing a predecessor who resigned amid calls for a change in leadership, with the outgoing MP, Powell, citing that Jeremy Corbyn's position as Labour party leader had become "untenable".
Chelsea manager Conte believes there are six strong teams that can fight for the title, with his own team leading the Premier League with 59 points and 14 games remaining.
A dispersal order has been issued in Llangefni, allowing police to force troublemakers, particularly youths under 16, to leave the area and potentially ban them from returning for up to 24 hours.
Chelsea midfielder Lewis Baker is a target for Boro, according to manager Garry Monk, as the club also looks to build on their recent signing of Marten de Roon.
The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, a award for humorous children's books, is being relaunched in 2016 as part of Roald Dahl's centenary celebrations, with plans to ensure a "robust future" for the prize.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr, a 74-year-old white supremacist, was sentenced to death for the murders of three people, including a 14-year-old boy and his grandfather, outside Jewish sites in Kansas last year.

A city council plans to introduce a self-service bike scheme with 500 bikes located across the city, aiming to be larger than a previous pilot scheme that ended in 2011, with the goal of financing the scheme through sponsorship and no taxpayer cost.

West Ham's Diaf Sakho, a 27-year-old Senegal international, has returned to light training after undergoing back surgery and is essentially at the start of his own personal pre-season training schedule.
According to the NI Residential Property Price Index, property prices in Northern Ireland rose by 5.4% annually in the third quarter, but only increased by 0.8% compared to the previous quarter.

A delivery of a huge wind turbine part on a country road in Dumfries and Galloway ended in an accident, where the lorry and its cargo ended up in a ditch, in contrast to a successful delivery at the same bridge just a few months earlier.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is considering downgrading services at some of its district hospitals due to staffing shortages, prompting a public consultation and meetings, despite concerns from residents that this could lead to longer travel times for maternity care.
South Africa's Mignon du Preez scored 116 off 99 balls to lead her team to a 272-6 total, which ultimately resulted in a win over Ireland by 68 runs, after Ireland was bowled out for 204.

Peake, a 30-year-old Welsh athlete, aims to break her own Welsh record and qualify for Team GB at the Rio Olympics by achieving a personal best height of at least 4.50m at the Cardiff International Sports Stadium.
A fire that burned for over 10 hours at a building site in Llanwern, Wales, is believed to have been deliberately set, with police investigating the circumstances surrounding the blaze.
A charity event, organized by Mercy Corps with local partners, was held in Edinburgh to raise money and support for the relief efforts following the devastating earthquake in Nepal.

Uefa has imposed a suspension on Hibernian head coach Neil Lennon for "acts of violence against the referee" during a Europa League qualifying match against Brondby, and Hibernian are currently appealing the decision.

A fire broke out at the ICL UK Boulby mine, one of Europe's deepest mines, on April 13, resulting in seven workers being treated for smoke inhalation and prompting a notice from the Health and Safety Executive to improve procedures.

Two men, including a 23-year-old British national, were removed from Machu Picchu in Peru after being caught posing naked, and the British Foreign Office is in contact with local authorities over the incident.
Croatian international Ivan Rakitic is set to sign a new deal with Barcelona, reportedly worth a £109m buyout clause, on Friday.

A couple from Halstead suffered life-changing injuries during a two-hour home invasion on April 26, and police have released a computer-generated image of one suspect, a black man of medium height, as they continue to investigate the crime.

The Wickerman Festival, taking place on July 25 and 26 near Dundrennan, Scotland, has announced its lineup, featuring Dizzee Rascal as the opening night headliner alongside other acts including Martha Reeves and The Vandellas and Big Country.
England hopeful Tom Foden expressed hope that his strong performance and that of his Northampton Saints team could bring out the best in him and potentially lead to more England squad selections.

A 22-year-old motorcyclist died after a collision involving a KTM motorcycle and a Vauxhall Zafira car in Dagenham, while a 7-year-old boy, who was a rear passenger in the car, remains in a serious condition.

Pfizer has agreed to acquire California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, the developer of eczema cream crisaborole, which is awaiting US FDA approval and has the potential for $2 billion in annual sales.
Police responded to a street fight in Dagenham, arresting two boys aged 17 and 15, and recovering several knives, scissors, and cannabis from the scene, with no reported injuries.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff has been arrested on suspicion of sexual assault after a 19-year-old woman reported an attack at Gorsedd Gardens near Cardiff Civic Centre on Thursday.

A by-election will be held in the Ettrick, Roxburgh and Berwickshire constituency in Scotland, following the resignation of Conservative MSP John Lamont, with the seat being contested for the Holyrood and Westminster representation.
The European Union has gained access to new markets for its beef exports, with Canada and the US now allowing imports from the EU, following the implementation of robust measures to eradicate BSE.

European finance ministers have endorsed a plan to create a unified EU list of "non-cooperative jurisdictions" by the end of summer, following the Panama Papers leak, and have also agreed to exchange information on beneficial company owners and crack down on banks and tax advisers who help clients hide money offshore.

Archaeologists working on the West Link road construction in Inverness, Scotland, have uncovered Bronze Age burnt mounds and other remains, including pottery fragments and kilns, which suggest ancient practices such as heating water for cooking and personal use.
Main scored for the Latics after the hour mark, securing a win that leaves Oldham with a significant cushion above the League One relegation places.
Colman Lally, a well-known Irish actor, passed away peacefully in hospital after a short illness, leaving behind his wife and three children.

Derby City Council has decided to keep Moorways Pool open for at least a year, after initially planning to close it due to budget cuts, following a successful petition by campaigners who highlighted the importance of the pool for local swimming programs and community use.
The UN has expressed concern that children previously held in areas controlled by Boko Haram in Nigeria may be being temporarily detained by the army without a proper legal process.
Hearts head coach Robbie Neilson is considering signing experienced goalkeeper Lee Hollis, who became a free agent after leaving Motherwell this summer.

Chelsey Lee, a 26-year-old American basketball player, is facing a lifetime suspension and record annulment in the Korean Women's Basketball League after allegations surfaced that she and her agents fabricated her birth certificate to claim South Korean heritage.

A new app has been released by UK regulator Ofcom to help people identify and improve their Wi-Fi speeds, which has found that six million homes and offices in the UK have slower Wi-Fi speeds than possible, and that despite progress in super-fast broadband availability, many rural areas and small businesses still lack access to high-speed internet.

Manchester United's forward Zlatan Ibrahimovic and midfielder Paul Pogba discussed the pressure of playing in the Premier League, with Ibrahimovic stating that top players are not affected by fan and press pressure, while Pogba thanked the supporters for their continued support after a 1-1 draw with Liverpool.

A 73-year-old fisherman in Brazil discovered a metal object, later confirmed to be a payload shroud from a European satellite launched last July, floating in a remote river and it took a team of over 10 people to retrieve it.

Former Labour government minister James Purnell warned that downgrading the licence fee to a civil offence could lead to increased non-payment and a £200m loss for the BBC, equivalent to the cost of removing channels like BBC Four, CBBC, and CBeebies from the air.
Harps earned their first win over Derry since 1998, with former Derry player Ryan Curran scoring the decisive goal in the 75th minute, as they secured a 2-1 victory in their Premier Division opener.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has announced that issuers of digital coins, known as Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs), must register their offers and sales in the same way as traditional securities sales to protect investors.

Operation Anagram, a police operation formed in 2006 to investigate serial killer Peter Tobin, has helped bring closure to the families of his victims, Vicky Hamilton and Dinah McNicol, by piecing together a timeline of his movements and relationships, although it continues to search for potential other unsolved crimes.

Mercedes driver Lewis Hamilton acknowledged that Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel's win in the Australian Grand Prix was well-deserved, but expressed optimism about Mercedes' chances to turn the tables at the Chinese race.

A woman has accused a former lawyer, who represented several high-profile celebrities, of indecent assault in his London office in the 1980s, with the alleged victim claiming she feared he would "rape or kill" her.
